meta.title: ZCHF compared: decentralized vs issuer-backed CHF stablecoins and USDC
meta.description: How Frankencoin (ZCHF) differs from issuer-backed Swiss franc stablecoins and from USDC: currency, backing, issuance and control, savings access, redemption.

hero.title: How ZCHF|differs.
hero.subtitle: Not every Swiss franc stablecoin works the same way. The main difference is whether a company issues it against bank deposits, or a protocol issues it against on-chain collateral.

head: ZCHF (Frankencoin)
Issuer-backed CHF stablecoins
USDC
rows: Over-collateralized BTC, ETH, gold and shares, visible on-chain

Cash and US treasuries held by Circle, per its attestations
Minted by anyone against collateral; rules set by FCS (Frankencoin Shares) holders; no freeze function

Issued by Circle, which can freeze addresses
Protocol savings rate, set by governance
No issuer to redeem with; peg held by collateral and arbitrage

note: The middle column groups several issuer-backed Swiss franc tokens; their reserves, terms and eligibility differ from issuer to issuer.

tradeoff.title: The trade-off
tradeoff.body: An issuer-backed token gives you a company to redeem with and a company that can freeze you. ZCHF gives you neither: nobody can block your balance, and its one-franc value rests on over-collateralization and the market rather than on a redemption promise.
